To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the YKFIR compensator is the only adaptive feedforward noise compensation algorithm able to provide an effective noise compensation in the case of a propagation delay in the secondary path larger than the one in the primary path.

the YKFIR adaptive compensator is the only one able to deal with the delay barrier in active noise control and that the YKF IR adaptive compensator outperforms the standard FIR adaptive compensation algorithms.

the Youla Kacura finite impulse response (FIR) adaptive compensators and the stability based FIR adaptive compensators using a filtered adaptation (FIRUSBA) are the only two algorithms that can be applied in the case where the secondary path is larger than the primary path.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an adaptive feedforward compensator that is stable even when the propagation delays of the primary path and of the secondary path are of the same order.
the design and the implementation of a new adaptive feedforward compensator that can overcome the delay barrier.
the development of a new class of adaptive feedforward algorithms for active noise control that can be used in the presence of a large delay of the secondary loop.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, when the secondary path delay is larger than the primary path one, only the YKFIR adaptive feedforward compensator is able to provide an efficient noise attenuation.

the YKFIR adaptive feedforward compensator is the only algorithm that provides a stable and efficient compensation in the case where the propagation delay of secondary path is larger than the one for the primary path.
in the case of a large secondary path, only the Youla Kecura finite impulse response adaptive compensator is suitable for adaptive feedforward active sound control applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the YKFIR algorithm is the most suitable for adaptive feedforward active control of broadband noise.
the YKFIR adaptive compensator is the most robust algorithm in the presence of a large secondary path.
the YKFIR adaptive compensator can be used in the context of large secondary paths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is necessary to develop a new algorithm for active feedforward compensation when the propagation delay of both paths is of the same order.
the use of a stability based filtered update is not sufficient to overcome the delay problem in feedforward adaptive control.

the YKFIR compensator is the only algorithm able to provide stable and efficient active feedforward noise compensation when the delay of the secondary loop is larger than the delay of the primary loop.
